newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Prazska Energetika sees lower 1997 net.
newsitem.headline: Prazska Energetika sees lower 1997 net.

text.p: Prague-based power distributor Prazska Energetika a.s. expects 1997 after-tax profit to drop to 254 million crowns from 322 million in 1996, the company's spokesman Jan Dolezalek told Reuters.
"Net profit should fall mainly due to the planned investment into the distribution network," he said.

Shareholders of the company, in which the state-run National Property Fund owns a controlling stake, voted on Wednesday to reinvest all 1996 net profit, rejecting the board's original proposal for a 25 crown gross dividend.
Dolezalek declined comment on a possible dividend forecast on 1997 profits.
He said that his company had not recorded a fall in demand as was reported earlier this year by the country's largest energy generator CEZ a.s..
"We have not registered so far a drop in demand, but we shall see what is the effect of the July deregulation of (electricty) prices," Dolezalek said.
The finance ministry plans an average hike in state-controlled electricty prices of 15 percent for household clients from July 1.
Household and small business clients comprise roughly one-third of Prazska Energetika's business.
